source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:1 ('בראשית ברא אלהים — the final letters are אמת: He created the world with TRUTH, as it says, the head of Your word is truth')
claim_en: THE FINALS OF TRUTH: the Torah's first three words — 'In the beginning God created' — end in the letters tav, aleph, mem (DB-checked in order): the letters of אמת ('truth'), the Kitzur reading the world created with truth sealed into the openings' own ends, as the psalm says 'the head of Your word is truth.'

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:1 ('בראשית — the bet DAGESHED, with tipcha under the shin; the bet is LARGE, standing at the head of the line and the head of the page — the bet of Blessed-is-His-Name')
claim_en: THE GREAT BET'S VERIFIED COMPANIONS: the Torah's first letter — the famous LARGE bet of בראשית — belongs to the uninstrumented letter-size layer, but its two ruled companions stand in the stream exactly as Minchat Shai gives them: the bet dageshed and the tipcha under the shin (DB-checked); the largeness itself, and the head-of-line head-of-page placement, filed to the letter-size and layout gaps as the layers' most famous members.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:3 ('יהי אור — with GALGAL and without maqqef: so the early print, the books of Spain, and BEN ASHER; Ben Naphtali reads maqqef and no galgal — and this is the FIRST of the differences between the two masters of the Masorah; we rely on Ben Asher's reading, as did the Rambam')
claim_en: LET THERE BE LIGHT — THE FIRST SPLIT OF THE TWO SCHOOLS: at the Torah's first command the two heads of the Masorah part for the first time — Ben Asher reads יהי unjoined with the wheel-accent, Ben Naphtali joins it to the light with maqqef. SNAPSHOT stands with BEN ASHER: no maqqef on the command (DB-checked), the Rambam's chosen reading — while the fulfillment ויהי־אור IS joined (builder-checked), command free and fulfillment bound; the wheel itself is stored as munach, the galgal class's fourth station, at the most famous site it will ever have.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:5 ('אור is written FIVE times in the section — against the five fifths of the Torah, which is called light')
claim_en: THE FIVE LIGHTS OF THE FIRST DAY: the light-word אור stands exactly FIVE times in the light-section (1:3 twice, 1:4 twice, 1:5 once — builder-counted): the Kitzur sets the five against the five books of the Torah, which is itself called light — the day-one word already carrying the whole shelf.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:4 ('את האור כי טוב — the final letters are ברית; and from here, that one does not bless over the flame until he can make use of its light')
claim_en: THE COVENANT AT THE ENDS OF THE LIGHT-CLAUSE: the four words 'the light, that it was good' (1:4) end in tav, resh, yod, bet (DB-checked in order) — the letters of ברית ('covenant'): the Kitzur reading the covenant sealed at the ends of the first thing called good, with the havdalah-flame teaching carried beside it, named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:2 ('ורוח אלהים — the Baal HaTurim's Masorah-pair as printed cites the spirit that CLOTHED Amasai; a corrupted copy stood before him — the true partner is the spirit that clothed ZECHARIAH (II Chr 24), as R. Meir Angel wrote') + Kitzur 1:2 ('מרחפת — in its count: this is the spirit of Messiah')
claim_en: THE HOVERING SPIRIT, ONCE: the pair ורוח אלהים ('and the SPIRIT OF GOD was hovering over the face of the waters') stands exactly once in the Torah (DB-checked); its Scripture partner in the construct-pair Masorah is the spirit that clothed Zechariah (II Chr 24, named) — with Minchat Shai's own text-criticism preserved: the printed Baal HaTurim cites Amasai, and Minchat Shai proves the copy corrupt and restores Zechariah. The Kitzur's Messiah-reading on the hovering, named beside it.
